hreflangReasoning: Thai is used as a first language essentially only in Thailand, so a language-only code is exact and future-proof; 'th-TH' would add nothing. Of the Thai competitor pages checked, klickpin.com, savepin.app and pindown.io declare 'th', dlpanda.com declares 'th-TH', and pinterestdownloader.io declares the invalid 'th-04' (and canonicalises to its English root, so it cannot rank in Thai). Each Thai page lists itself (th), its English twin (en) and x-default (English). Skipped pages get no th alternate. Set <html lang="th"> and og:locale 'th_TH'.

markets.notes: Single market. Thai searchers mix scripts freely: the brand is almost always typed in Latin ('pinterest'), verbs and nouns in Thai ('โหลด', 'รูป', 'วิดีโอ'), and device or format words in Latin or Thai ('iphone'/'ไอโฟน', 'pc'/'คอม', 'gif', 'mp4'). Autocomplete under hl=th also returns English queries, which the English pages already serve.

urlStructure.pattern: /th/<slug>; homepage is /th with no trailing slash (normalizeCanonical in src/lib/urls.ts).
urlStructure.slugPolicy: Keep the English slug for every Thai page except one (below). Thai script cannot be used (ASCII-only rule), and RTGS romanisation of the Thai keywords ('lot-witdio-pinterest', 'load-roop') is something no Thai user reads or types. The Latin words Thai searchers really type (pinterest, video, gif, mp4, iphone, android, chrome) are already in the English slugs. Keeping them also makes /th/<enSlug> routing and hreflang pairing mechanical.

keptEnglishSlugDespiteMismatch: how-to-download-pinterest-video-on-laptop: Thai says 'คอม', not 'laptop'. The title and H1 carry 'คอม'; the URL is not worth breaking parity for.

claimTicket.concept: Thais know the cloakroom/claim stub ('ต้นขั้ว') and, even more, the numbered queue ticket ('บัตรคิว' at banks, clinics, government offices). The ticket conceit translates well if labels stay short and functional.
claimTicket.ticket: ตั๋ว (colloquial, playful) rather than บัตร (formal). Use as a visual noun, not in instructions.
claimTicket.Admit one · public link: '1 ลิงก์ 1 สิทธิ์ · สาธารณะเท่านั้น' - riffs on the familiar Thai slogan pattern '1 คน 1 สิทธิ์' (one person, one entitlement). Natural, short, keeps 'admit one' wit. Plainer fallback: 'ตั๋ว 1 ใบ · ลิงก์สาธารณะ'.
claimTicket.No. (serial): Keep 'No.' in the Latin gothic (Thai tickets and receipts print 'No.' too), or 'เลขที่' if the label must be Thai.

formats.numerals: Western digits (0-9). Thai digits (๐-๙) only in formal government documents; never in UI.
formats.thousandsDecimal: 1,234.5 (comma thousands, point decimal), same as en.
formats.units: Space before Latin units: '12.4 MB', '1080p', '600×600 พิกเซล'.
formats.counts: Thai has no plural; numbers take classifiers: '250 พิน', '3 ขั้นตอน', 'ไฟล์ ZIP 1 ไฟล์', 'รูปที่ 2 จาก 5'. ICU plural rules for th have only 'other'.
formats.dates: Thai readers expect the Buddhist Era: 2026 CE = พ.ศ. 2569. Intl.DateTimeFormat('th-TH') uses the Buddhist calendar by default: medium '15 ต.ค. 2569', long '15 ตุลาคม 2569'. Keep JSON-LD datePublished/dateModified in ISO 8601 (Gregorian). Do not put a year in titles: autocomplete shows both systems ('เซฟ รูป จาก pinterest 2566' is BE, 'โหลดรูป pinterest ไม่ชัด 2024' is CE), so any year halves the match.
formats.punctuation: No full stop at the end of Thai sentences; a space separates sentences and phrases. '?' is acceptable in FAQ headings (every Thai competitor uses it) but not needed in body text. Repetition mark: write 'ชัด ๆ' (Royal Institute) or avoid it in titles. Quotes: “ ”.
formats.currency: None needed (free). If ever: '฿99' or '99 บาท'.

typography.fontCoverage: Big Shoulders Display has NO Thai glyphs (Google Fonts serves only latin, latin-ext and vietnamese subsets; checked css2 API). Thai headlines would fall back to whatever the OS has (Thonburi on iOS/macOS, Noto Sans Thai on Android, Leelawadee UI or Tahoma on Windows), mismatched in weight and width.
typography.recommendedHeadlineFont: Noto Sans Thai (Google Fonts, OFL), variable with wdth 62.5-100% and wght 100-900, with a 'thai' subset (unicode-range U+0E01-0E5B, U+200C-200D, U+25CC). Use it at font-stretch ~75% and weight 800-900: a loopless, condensed Thai gothic that sits next to Big Shoulders. Keep Big Shoulders Display FIRST in the stack. Its unicode-range excludes Thai, so Latin words (PINTEREST, MP4, GIF, ZIP) stay in Big Shoulders and Thai characters fall through to Noto Sans Thai. Self-host only the thai-subset woff2 next to the existing /fonts/big-shoulders-* files and preload it on /th pages only. Alternative: Kanit 800/900 (the most common Thai display face), but it is not condensed.
typography.bodyFont: Keep the system stack for body text (Thai system fonts are good, and it costs no bytes); add 'Noto Sans Thai', 'Leelawadee UI', 'Thonburi', Tahoma before sans-serif for Windows coverage.
typography.lineHeight: The display line-height of 0.88-0.9 WILL collide or clip Thai: tone marks stack above upper vowels (ที่, นี้, ปุ่ม) and lower vowels hang below the baseline (ดู, ปุ, ฤ). Use about 1.2-1.3 for Thai display/headlines, about 1.7 for body. Check that no hero container uses overflow:hidden with tight heights.
typography.letterSpacing: Set letter-spacing: 0 under :lang(th) for label (0.08em), serial (0.04em) and stamps; tracking pulls Thai syllable clusters apart.
typography.case: Thai has no case, so text-transform: uppercase only shouts the Latin tokens ('PINTEREST'). Either accept the mixed look (common on Thai posters) or set text-transform: none for :lang(th) headings so 'Pinterest' reads as the brand. The ticket's punch must come from weight and condensed width, not caps.
typography.lineBreaking: Thai has no spaces between words; browsers break lines with an ICU dictionary. Never use word-break: keep-all on Thai (no break opportunities, so it overflows). Avoid overflow-wrap: anywhere on Thai text (it can split inside a syllable); keep it only on URLs. Write H1s with natural phrase spaces ('โหลดวิดีโอ Pinterest ลงมือถือ') so breaks land between phrases; use <wbr> if a long H1 breaks badly at 360px.
typography.lengthVsLatin: Thai strings are usually SHORTER on screen than their English source: combining vowels and tone marks are separate code points with no advance width. A 60-code-point Thai title is roughly 45-50 visible glyph columns. The repo's 40-62 / 120-158 limits count code points (Python len), so they are conservative for Thai: Google's pixel-based truncation leaves room. All kept titles here are 49-61 code points and descriptions 131-154.
typography.smallSizes: Gothic 800 at 0.875rem gets blotchy in Thai (tight counters). Use 600-700 weight for Thai labels at that size, or bump to 0.9375rem.
typography.encoding: Store NFC; write SARA AM as U+0E33 'ำ' (not U+0E4D + U+0E32, which Google's suggestion feed prints); no zero-width spaces in <title> or meta (they count toward length and can split matches). The build script checks both.

notes: Kept 13 of 19 pages. Priority 1: index, video, image. Priority 2: HD (ex-4K), GIF, board, how-to hub, mobile (absorbs gallery), computer. Priority 3: pin, profile picture, audio, Chrome.

Skipped 6: profile-downloader (no Thai demand), carousel (Thai queries are about creating multi-image pins), story (no demand; Idea Pins folded into regular pins), to-mp4 (folded into video), seo-title-generator (tool outputs English only; un-skip when it supports lang=th), gallery guide (merged into the mobile page).

Biggest Thai-specific opportunity: the 'ไม่ชัด / ให้ชัด' (blurry/sharp) cluster, which shows up under nearly every image seed and has no honest competitor page. It goes on the reframed HD page, so the image page should not also target 'ให้ชัด' as a keyword.
Second opportunity: device-specific how-tos. 'ios', 'android', 'iphone', 'pc', 'mac', 'ในคอม', 'ลงไอแพด' are first-level completions of the head terms. iPad comes up far more than in Western markets.
Teach the Pinterest 'บันทึก' trap on every how-to: in Pinterest Thai, 'บันทึก' saves to a board. Users search 'บันทึกวิดีโอ pinterest' expecting a device save; Pinterest's own help draws the line.

Honesty blockers found in the product while researching: (1) the 'MP3' download is the video file renamed .mp3 (DownloaderForm.tsx ~L966/~L2072); the Thai audio page avoids promising MP3 until that is fixed. (2) The English 4K page promises '4K ultra quality', which PRODUCT.md forbids; the Thai twin is reframed and re-slugged. (3) Current th i18n heroSubtitle says 'ความละเอียด HD 1080p' for images and boards, which is not generally true.

Brand-confusion risk: 'pindownload.io' ranks for 'โหลดวิดีโอ pinterest' in Thailand and differs from PintDownload by one letter. Thai users read Latin brand names loosely. Show the full domain 'pintdownload.app' on /th and in the Organization schema 'name'/'alternateName'.

Thai copy must be native, not translated from the English pages. Competitors' machine-translated Thai ('ไม่ KlickPin ทำงานบนมือถือ?') is the norm, and it reads badly. Have a native Thai reader check the final pages, especially the how-to steps against a Thai-language Pinterest app (the 'คัดลอกลิงก์' label is not yet verified on a device).
Internal links: /th links only to /th pages and to the /th hub for link types without a Thai page (profile ZIP, carousel, story). Do not send Thai users to English pages mid-flow.

Rank tracking: check positions with gl=th & hl=th; a US-located check misses most Thai SERP features. Thai SERPs for the head terms mix tool pages, how-to guides (wikiHow TH, tecnobits, guru99 TH) and a Play Store app.

SERP sampling was limited: DuckDuckGo (kl=th-th) answered one query before rate-limiting, and Bing/DDG-lite returned challenge pages. Competitor evidence therefore comes mostly from fetching their Thai pages directly. Re-check SERPs from a Thai IP before launch if possible.
